## What changed

**The tool now reads `/etc/gitlab/gitlab.rb` for settings a version on the path
will refuse.** This is the actual cause of the failure that 0.1.15 addressed the
*consequences* of. Step 7 of a 19-step climb (15.11.13) died inside
`reconfigure`, not in apt:

```
gitlab_rails['smtp_tls'] and gitlab_rails['smtp_enable_starttls_auto']
are mutually exclusive. Set one of them to false.
```

That combination had been sitting in `gitlab.rb` for years. GitLab 13.12 accepts
it; `SmtpHelper.validate_smtp_settings!` was added later and rejects it. The
refusal happens *after* the package is installed, so the package is left
unconfigured, the migrations never run, and the next backup fails against the
old schema.

Nothing about that needed to be discovered at step 7. The setting is in a file,
and the version that starts rejecting it is knowable. A readiness check now
names both, before the first backup:

```
✗  gitlab.rb   smtp_tls и smtp_enable_starttls_auto включены оба — с 15.11.4
               reconfigure это отвергает, подъём оборвётся на шаге
               15.11.13-ee.0; оставьте одно: smtp_tls для порта 465,
               smtp_enable_starttls_auto для 587
```

The rules live in `data/gitlab-rb-conflicts.json` and each one is checked
against omnibus-gitlab source at specific tags, not against the docs — the docs
do not say which version introduced a validation. For this rule:
`smtp_helper.rb` is present at tag `15.11.4+ee.0` and absent at `15.11.3+ee.0`,
and the commit reached master for 16.0.0, so a single threshold of 15.11.4 is
exact. A test refuses any rule that lacks a source link, a threshold note, a
finding text in both locales, and a remedy entry.

Two deliberate limits. Only settings the file sets to a literal `true`
count — a check that stops a healthy server because it misread a line gets
waived along with every other check, and then it catches nothing. And only the
listed keys are read, with `grep`, never the whole file: `gitlab.rb` holds the
SMTP password and tokens, and a failing command's output is written to disk.
An unreadable `gitlab.rb` is a warning, not an all-clear.
